subject: Locality cutover windows, subprocessor sequencing, and temporary egress policy
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Locality cutover windows & subprocessor sequencing - request

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we map out our migration plan for onboarding Redwood for EU production, Legal and Infra asked for a short, concrete schedule: a proposed cutover/toggle timetable for region-anchoring, and an ordered list of subprocessors that may be activated during the first 90 days.

Two specific asks from our side:
1) A week-by-week cutover window (UTC) showing when traffic will begin routing to EU-only tenants vs when short-lived telemetry/analytics bursts might cross the border for up to X hours.
2) A sequencing list for subprocessors (analytics, monitoring, telemetry, cloud-burst compute) with the earliest activation dates and any expected transient egress.

We also need to understand how Redwood will signal a temporary egress event (e.g., failover to US for 48h) — what controls do we get (opt-in toggle, notification channels, audit evidence)?

Can you share a draft timetable and the subprocessor roster (even if redacted for versions)? We need this to finalize the DPA annex and our internal risk acceptance before the procurement signatures.

Appreciate it — Sam
Data Privacy Officer, Acme Health

---
Attachments: none
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Locality cutover windows & subprocessor sequencing - request

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a working roster and a proposed cutover timetable that aligns with our standard EU anchoring playbook. High level notes inline: 

- Cutover approach:
  * Day 0 (week 0) — soft switch: application routing affinity set to EU region, read-only analytics replicated but not processed outside EU.
  * Week 1 — operational monitoring services (metrics/alerts) enabled; they use truncated telemetry and are routed to EU ops endpoints.
  * Weeks 2–4 — scheduled activation of non-critical subprocessors (e.g., third-party telemetry enrichers). All activations include a documented transient-egress window of no more than 4 hours per activation for key syncs.
  * Months 2–3 — full activation of burst capacity (US-backed GPU pools) only if explicitly authorized and documented in the change record.

- Failover & temporary egress:
  * We provide an opt-in emergency failover toggle for customers with a signed annex. When triggered, the system records an audit event, dispatches email/SMS notifications to your SRE and Security contacts, and emits a compliance-ready log bundle (signed timestamp).

- Signaling and evidence: each transient egress includes: start/end timestamps, affected resource IDs, list of subprocessors activated, and a zipped audit bundle stored for your review in the drive link below.

Ive attached: subprocessor_roster_20270424.pdf (redacted addresses, includes activation buckets) and cutover_timetable_v2.xlsx (UTC windows). Marissa is copied to confirm sequencing and the ops constraints.

If useful, we can schedule a short runbook walkthrough with Infra and Legal this week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20270424.pdf (PDF, 48KB); cutover_timetable_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Locality cutover windows & subprocessor sequencing - draft operational notes

Sam / Team — a few operational clarifications from infra before you finalize the annex: 

1) Subprocessor activation buckets: we index subprocessors into three buckets 
   - Bucket A (EU-hosted): core data plane, KV storage, EU observability collectors — no egress.
   - Bucket B (EU-primary, transient sync): enrichment services that need a one-time sync (we limit syncs to 4h windows; we publish the exact UTC start times).
   - Bucket C (Burst/Failover US-backed): GPU burst pools / CDN edge that may process content outside EU when explicitly authorized.

2) Our default policy for Bucket B is to do the one-time sync within maintenance windows (02:00–06:00 UTC) and to throttle any cross-border payloads to metadata-only where possible.

3) KMS & keying: customer-controlled KMS can be used for sensitive fields. If you enable a split-KMS workflow we can guarantee key material never leaves EU. However, logs/metrics that are not customer-secret may still have routing metadata and short-lived telemetry in failover.

4) Audit deliverables: we can produce a single zipped evidence bundle per declared transient-egress event, plus a monthly summary report. If you need higher retention for audit, we can push a custom retention policy in the annex.

Notes for Legal: we recommend calling out: maximum duration per transient egress event, notification SLA (15 min), and whether you want an automated rollback within X hours.

Happy to run this in a short working session with Acme Infra — propose Wed 2027-04-28 08:00–09:00 UTC.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Locality cutover windows & subprocessor sequencing - ops checklist

Looping in an ops checklist so Acme has concrete gating criteria for each activation: 
- Pre-activation checklist (for any Bucket B/C activation): config snapshot, artifact hashes, KMS policy applied, legal sign-off flag present, and a pre-flight smoke test in EU-only mode (10 min).
- Activation runbook will include: UTC start, expected duration, rollback command, and a one-click audit export endpoint we will hand you (a signed JSON with timestamps).
- If the customer requests an automated rollback on threshold (e.g., error rate > 3% for 10m), we can wire that into the change.

Sam — can you confirm the internal Acme sign-off roles (who will approve per-activation: Infra lead, Security lead)? We will add them to the notification list.

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Locality cutover windows & subprocessor sequencing - ack and next steps

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick answers: 
- Approvers: Infra lead (Lena Ortiz), Security lead (Sam Patel — me), plus Legal (contract sign-off). Lena is cc'd.
- We accept the Bucket model, and will ask Legal to add the max-duration-per-event and 15-minute notification SLA into the DPA annex.
- Wed 2027-04-28 08:00–09:00 UTC works for a run-through; please send a calendar invite.

Please also add one request to the annex: evidence retention for transient-egress events must be retained for 12 months.

Appreciate you moving quickly on this — Sam
Data Privacy Officer, Acme Health
